Title: Melaka BN told not to underestimate rivals in state election
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Melaka Barisan Nasional candidates and election machinery have been reminded not to become complacent or underestimate their opponents in the upcoming state election on Nov 14.
Its chairman, Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh, said BN's journey to where it is today was not easy, adding that current achievements stemmed from hard work, stability, and public support.
Therefore, he said BN must continue focusing on resolving issues faced by the people and maintaining the stability built over the years.
"Never become complacent. Do not underestimate the opposition. Continue going to the ground and listening to the voices of the people.
"Our opponents also have strengths, but as I often say, if they give, we take! If they want to contribute, we take!" he said on his Facebook page last night.
Earlier, Rauf launched the Kota Melaka parliamentary-level BN election machinery for the 16th Melaka election and joined a motorcycle convoy of more than 100 riders to the launch site at Taman Bukit Punggur, Telok Mas.
He said he had concluded the announcement of BN candidates for the state election the night before and urged all leadership levels and party machinery to help ensure their victory, including Duyong candidate Datuk Mohd Noor Helmy Abdul Halem and Datuk Abdul Razak Abdul Rahman (Telok Mas).
"Melaka is the bridge to Putrajaya. On Nov 14, let us unite, Malays, Chinese, Indians, and all the people of Melaka, for a more glorious future for the state," he said.
The coalition announced 21 candidates for the 16th Melaka election, fielding eight new faces and retaining 13 incumbents.
The candidates comprise 18 from Umno, two from MCA, and one from MIC, with seven remaining seats to be allocated to strategic partners working together in the state election.

Title: Police bust online gaming scam syndicate operating from abandoned hotel
Article:
SUNGAI PETANI: Police have dismantled an online gaming scam syndicate masterminded by Bangladeshi citizens operating out of an abandoned hotel in Taman Lagenda Indah here.
The 9.30pm raid on Wednesday led to the arrest of four Bangladeshi men, aged between 30 and 53, believed to be working for the syndicate.
Kuala Muda district police chief Assistant Commissioner Hanyan Ramlan said the syndicate is believed to have operated since June, using a dedicated website and WhatsApp to communicate with clients, also believed to be Bangladeshi nationals.
He said the operation was uncovered following public tip-offs regarding suspicious movements at the hotel premises, which had been defunct since 2022.
"Checks revealed that the premises were used as a call centre handling top-ups for online gaming points tied to non-existent monetary rewards.
"The syndicate is believed to have targeted between 18 and 50 customers daily.
"Preliminary findings show that about 17 customer accounts a day faced delayed withdrawals, resulting in them not receiving the promised money, with estimated losses of about RM2,000 a day. The total actual losses are still being verified," he said at a press conference at the Kuala Muda district police headquarters yesterday.
Hanyan said the four detained Bangladeshi men each earned about RM2,700 per month.
Police also seized 17 mobile phones, four computer processing units, eight monitors, two modems, a laptop, and RM2,442 in cash.
"The total value of the seized items is estimated at RM18,000," he said.
Hanyan said police arrested two local men, aged between 40 and 50, two days ago, who were believed to be involved in renting out the premises.
He said one of them is believed to be the property owner, while the other acted as an agent or broker managing the rental.
"Police are also investigating the possibility of other parties assisting the syndicate with facilities, including the rental of the premises.
"While the total actual losses remain under investigation, police will collaborate with relevant agencies to inspect the electricity supply status at the premises to determine if any illegal connections were made.
"Police are also scrutinising the background and entry routes of the foreigners into the country, including their purpose of coming to Malaysia," he said.
He said the case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code for cheating and Section 120B of the same code for criminal conspiracy.
He advised the public to remain vigilant against unrealistic offers of cash returns or online rewards, and to verify details before making financial transactions.

Title: Police advise public to avoid Bagan Lalang beach over crocodile sighting
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Visitors to Pantai Bagan Lalang have been advised to avoid beach activities following reports of a suspected crocodile sighting in the area.
Sepang district police chief Assistant Commissioner Norhizam Bahaman said police received a report yesterday afternoon of an animal believed to be a crocodile spotted near a beach resort.
"For the safety of residents and tourists, police advise the public to refrain from activities along Bagan Lalang beach in Sungai Pelek," he said in a statement today.
Norhizam said police will collaborate with relevant agencies to monitor the situation and take appropriate measures to ensure public safety.

Title: PH banks on track record in three states to win Melaka
Article:
MELAKA: Pakatan Harapan is banking on its experience governing Selangor, Penang and Negri Sembilan as it seeks to win over voters in the Nov 14 Melaka election.
Prime Minister's political secretary Datuk Azman Abidin said PH had experience managing the administrations in the three states and hoped Melaka voters would give the coalition the same opportunity.
He said PH believed its governing experience could serve as a foundation for leading Melaka.
"We know PH has a good track record, having successfully managed the administrations in Selangor, Penang and Negri Sembilan.
"If the people of Melaka give us the opportunity to lead the state, God willing, we will do our best, just as we have done in Selangor, Penang and Negri Sembilan," he said after the closing ceremony of Minggu Melaka Ceria in Tanjung Minyak last night.
Azman said PH's main aim was to give voters a choice in deciding which party should lead the state.
On Saturday, PH chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced the coalition's 21 candidates for the Melaka polls, with PKR contesting nine seats, DAP seven and Amanah five.

Title: Lula defies odds to win fourth term as Brazil president
Article:
RIO DE JANEIRO: Brazil's leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva pulled off a dramatic comeback on Sunday as he clinched election victory against right-wing senator Flavio Bolsonaro, who trounced him in the first round.
The leftist icon, who turns 81 on Tuesday, defied all projections to win an unprecedented fourth term at the helm of Latin America's largest country.
According to official results, he won 51.75 per cent of the votes to 48.25 per cent for Flavio Bolsonaro, son of former far-right president Jair Bolsonaro, who had entered election day confident with his lead in the polls.
With Lula's victory, Brazil staved off a conservative wave that has seen numerous countries – such as Argentina, Chile, Colombia, and Peru – all shift right, backed by US President Donald Trump.
After a campaign marred by scandal and mud-slinging, Sunday's vote plunged into chaos after a last-minute Supreme Court ruling extending voting by two hours, at the request of Lula who said buses had been pulled from circulation in various cities, barring citizens from voting.
Flavio Bolsonaro also requested an extension in some parts of the country due to heavy rains, but his camp lashed out at the country-wide extension.
"Either we win. Or we win. Consider yourself warned," pro-Bolsonaro lawmaker Nikolas Ferreira wrote on X as the votes streamed in.
The bitter campaign laid bare the deep divisions in the country of over 200 million people.
"It's a disgrace. We've never had anything like this in Brazil, and now they've come up with the idea of extending the election period by two hours," said Aurelio Junior, 45, a dentist in Brasilia.
Jacqueline Maria Lima de Franca, 34, a business owner in Rio de Janeiro backing Lula said it was "more than fair...everyone should have the right to vote, and that was being neglected."
- LULA RISES FROM THE ASHES, AGAIN -
Lula, a defining figure in Brazilian politics over four decades, was blindsided after his first-round defeat to Bolsonaro.
The left swung into action with massive rallies declaring "Never Again Bolsonaro," where protesters recalled the former president's chaotic handling of the Covid pandemic, devastation of the Amazon rainforest and cuts to public programs.
Lula also revamped his social media strategy, taking video selfies and even bought his first cellphone, while supporters carried out a feverish campaign to change the minds of family, friends and neighbors, and encourage them to vote after high levels of abstention.
His re-election marks another remarkable comeback for the man who grew up dirt poor in the northeast in a family of illiterate farmers.
Lula, revered for social welfare programs that lifted millions out of poverty, made a dramatic return to office in 2022 elections after a corruption scandal saw him jailed for over 18 months.
The charges, annulled on procedural grounds, have continued to haunt him.
In his third term he has overseen a drop in inflation and unemployment, and lifted millions out of hunger, but voters complain about the cost of living and a sense of insecurity.
Lula's social policies became a point of tension as he expanded welfare programs during the campaign.
"Brazil needs more time with Lula, primarily because the country is on the verge of falling into the clutches of fascism," Maria Fernanda Elisbao, a 21-year-old editorial assistant, told AFP.
- A TRICKY TERM AHEAD -
Lula heads into a fourth term with a country divided, with almost half of the nation voting against him and desperate for change.
"We're in a deep hole, things are dire. People can barely afford to eat – buying meat is out of the question," said Tereza Cristina Ramos, a 68-year-old retiree, who voted in Rio de Janeiro.
Already one of the world's oldest leaders, Lula will be 85 by the end of his new term in 2030.
He will thus have spent 16 years in power, following his first stint as president from 2003 to 2010.
Lula is also facing a hostile Congress dominated by the right.
His options are also constrained by the economic outlook, with growth expected to slow.
He has also come under renewed pressure to confront rampant insecurity in a country plagued by criminal factions that sow terror in working-class neighbourhoods.
The president's campaign leaned heavily on the theme of sovereignty in the face of commercial and diplomatic pressure from Trump's United States.
Voters must "choose a country where the flag is respected," he said, his raspy voice more hoarse than ever after a tireless campaign. He accused his rival of wanting to "govern with the American flag."--AFP

Title: Storms wreak havoc across Europe, disrupting power, flights and phones
Article:
LONDON: Storms battered northern Europe Sunday, killing a man, cutting power to more than 150,000 homes and disrupting travel and phone networks.
A man died when a tree fell on him in southwestern Scotland, while a runner in a marathon in northern France was injured when a tree was felled by strong winds during the race.
More than 82,000 homes in Britain, nearly 60,000 in France and at least 10,000 in Germany had power cuts inflicted by the passage of storms Boelo and Austen within 24 hours of each other, authorities in the countries said.
In the Argyll and Bute region of western Scotland, winds of up to 135km an hour were recorded. Trees and power cables brought down by the storm blocked roads and rail lines across Scotland and northern England.
Britain's Energy Networks Association said more than 400,000 homes had lost power at some stage during the storms.
Part of the pier at Brighton on the southern England coast, unused since a fire in 2003, blew away in Storm Austen on Friday.
The powerful winds also battered northern France across the Channel as Europe battled its first big autumn storms of the year. Experts have warned of more extreme weather events because of global warming.
Authorities warned of flood risk in regions in Scotland and England.
A runner was lightly injured in the northern French city of Lille near the start of the city's marathon, which was being staged for the first time in 31 years.
- WIDESPREAD POWER CUTS -
French energy company Enedis said that at the peak of storm Austen on Saturday, some 288,000 homes had no electricity.
Some 59,000 remained without power at midday Sunday, mainly in Normandy and Brittany. It said 2,600 Enedis technicians and contractors were working to re-establish power.
In Germany, Austen cut power to 10,000 homes in and around the southwestern town of Freiburg-Brisgau on Sunday. The town's main hospital said it had to limit service to emergency cases because of the blackout that also cut the mobile phone network.
Two people were seriously hurt Saturday by scaffolding blown away by storm Austen's winds during an autumn market at the town of Nastatten, German police said.
Germany's DWD weather agency predicted more powerful winds of up to 100kph on the northern coast on Sunday.
The storms also hit the Netherlands and Belgium, where falling trees injured four people in Brussels on Saturday.
Hundreds of flights were cancelled or diverted because of the storms across northern Europe.
Amsterdam's Schiphol airport, one of Europe's busiest hubs, cancelled dozens of flights Sunday.
AFP counted some 90 flights cancelled on the airport website, mainly to European cities including Paris, Rome and Dublin. Dozens of flights due to land at the airport were also cancelled.
Flights in northern England and Scotland were also hit by the storms.--AFP

Title: Sarawak assembly dissolved, paving way for state election
Article:
KUCHING: The Sarawak assembly was officially dissolved today, paving the way for the 13th state election.
Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg
announced the dissolution
on Friday after receiving the consent of Sarawak Governor Tun Dr Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar.
Article 21(4) of the State Constitution stipulates that the state election must be held within 60 days of the dissolution.
Attention now turns to the Election Commission (EC) to set a date for a special meeting to determine key dates for the polls.
EC secretary Datuk Khairul Shahril Idrus said on Oct 23 that the commission would set the meeting date after receiving
formal notification
of the dissolution from the Speaker.
Meanwhile, Abang Johari, who is also Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) chairman, said the state government would continue operating as a caretaker government in accordance with constitutional requirements and conventions.
"Public administration and essential services will continue to ensure the needs and welfare of the people are safeguarded," he said.
The current term of the 82-seat assembly was due to expire in February 2027.
GPS won 76 of the 82 seats contested in the 12th Sarawak state election on Dec 18, 2021, while Parti Sarawak Bersatu (PSB) won four seats and DAP secured two.
Sarawak's political landscape changed after PSB was dissolved in 2024, with three of its former assemblymen joining Progressive Democratic Party (PDP), a component party of GPS.
Another former PSB assemblyman, See Chee How, who represents Batu Lintang, subsequently left the party and became an Independent.
GPS comprises Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB), Sarawak United Peoples' Party (SUPP), Parti Rakyat Sarawak (PRS) and PDP.

Title: 2,670 displaced in Israel's Hebron operation: Palestinian Authority
Article:
RAMALLAH: The Palestinian Authority said Sunday that nearly 2,700 people had been displaced by an Israeli military operation in the occupied West Bank city of Hebron launched after two soldiers were killed in an attack nearby.
Following Friday's attack, Israeli forces entered the Hebron neighbourhood of Ein Deir Baha, where the assailants lived, and ordered residents to pack up and leave after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu pledged a major operation in the occupied territory.
"More than 2,670 Palestinians have been forcibly displaced from their homes in Hebron by Israeli occupation forces, the majority of them women, children, and elderly people, according to data from Hebron Municipality," the Palestinian prime minister's office said on X.
A convoy of Israeli military and police vehicles accompanied by soldiers was seen in Hebron on Sunday, making its way down a street blocked to civilian traffic by parked cars and motorbikes, AFP images showed.
Local shopkeeper Higazi al-Tamimi, who also plays a leadership role in the evacuated neighbourhood, accused Israeli soldiers of beating him as he attempted to go to his home.
"I remember one or two people starting to strike my legs, chest and shoulders. One of them even hit me on the head," he said from a hospital bed, with his leg thickly bandaged.
"They then pushed me backwards, and I kept moving until I reached a safe area."--AFP

Title: Haze eases, most areas record good, moderate air quality
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Haze conditions across the country continued to improve, with most areas recording good or moderate Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 7am today.
According to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, 29 areas in Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak recorded good API readings, while 32 recorded moderate levels.
However, seven areas in Sarawak continued to record unhealthy air quality, with the Serian district police headquarters monitoring station registering the highest API reading at 173.
The other areas were Samarahan (160), Kuching (159), Sarikei (157), Sibu (154), Sri Aman (139) and Mukah (109).
An API reading of zero to 50 is classified as good, 51 to 100 as moderate, 101 to 200 as unhealthy, 201 to 300 as very unhealthy, and readings above 300 as hazardous.

Title: Ringgit higher against US dollar in early trade
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit was slightly higher against the US dollar in early trade on Monday amid cautious sentiment ahead of the US Federal Reserve's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on Oct 27-28.

Title: Student housing shortage, Syariah Court delays among Dewan Rakyat focus
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Strategies to strengthen downstream commodity industries, the shortage of accommodation at public university colleges and delays in Syariah Court proceedings are among the issues to be raised in the Dewan Rakyat today.
According to the Order Paper on Parliament's official website, Datuk Shamshulkahar Mohd Deli (BN-Jempol) will ask the plantation and commodities minister about strategies to strengthen downstream commodity industries.
This also includes strategies to increase the value of local products, reduce reliance on raw material exports and expand industrial opportunities and income for smallholders.
Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail (PH-Bandar Tun Razak) will ask the higher education minister about ongoing efforts to address the shortage of accommodation at public university residential colleges, particularly for students from the B40 income group.
Additionally, Zulkifli Ismail (PN-Jasin) will ask the prime minister to outline measures to address delays in Syariah Court proceedings, particularly cases involving maintenance and child-related claims that have remained unresolved for years.
Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias (BN-Jelebu) will ask the economy minister about the government's assessment of the challenges facing the middle-income group, including rising housing, education, healthcare and family-related expenses, despite some households not qualifying for assistance.
Following the question-and-answer session, the Dewan Rakyat is scheduled to continue the winding-up session at the policy stage on the Supply Bill 2027 by the relevant ministries.
The current Dewan Rakyat sitting will run for 37 days until Dec 8.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Oil slips from near six-months highs despite supply concerns
Article:
BEIJING: Oil prices fell on Monday after surging to near six-month highs late last week, although ongoing attacks on Saudi Arabia kept supply concerns in focus.
US crude futures were down US$1.60, or 1.55 per cent, at US$101.67 per barrel by 0018 GMT. Brent crude futures were down US$1.56 or 1.34 per cent at US$115.16.
Prices had settled nearly US$3 higher on Friday after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked energy supply concerns. Brent finished the week up six per cent and West Texas Immediate ended 2.3 per cent higher.
Attacks continued over the weekend with Houthis saying they had attacked the Saudi airport and oil facilities on Saturday. Saudi Arabia said on Sunday it had intercepted more missiles and drones.
The top oil exporter restarted partial operations at its main airport on Sunday after damage in a previous round of Houthi attacks even as the militant group vowed to keep targeting the facility.

Title: Two men held over nearly 20,000 sticks of smuggled cigarettes seized in Tanah Merah
Article:
TANAH MERAH: Two men, including a Pakistani, were arrested after nearly 20,000 sticks of smuggled cigarettes were seized in two separate raids yesterday.
The raids were conducted by the General Operations Force (GOF) 9th Battalion at Kampung Bukit Nangka and Kampung Paralla Dua between 4pm and 5pm following intelligence gathering.
Southeast Brigade GOF commander Datuk Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the first raid was conducted at a house in Kampung Bukit Nangka, Gual Ipoh, at 4pm.
He said officers arrested a 33-year-old local man after finding 6,080 sticks of smuggled cigarettes worth RM11,456 in a sack placed near a pile of wood in front of the house.
"The suspect claimed he obtained the cigarettes from an individual known as 'Chong' and intended to sell them around Tanah Merah," he said in a statement.
Radzi said the second raid was conducted at a shop-house in Kampung Paralla Dua at 5pm.
"An inspection of the premises uncovered a sack containing several cartons of smuggled cigarettes, totalling 13,880 sticks and worth more than RM26,000.
"We arrested a 55-year-old Pakistani man for further investigation. During questioning, he claimed the cigarettes had been supplied by two people who delivered them to the premises for sale and distribution," he said.
Both suspects were arrested under Section 135(1)(d) of the Customs Act.
Radzi said the suspects had been handed over to the Tanah Merah district police headquarters' Criminal Investigation Department for further investigation.
"The GOF will continue monitoring the border to prevent incursions and smuggling," he said.

Title: Trump says Canada tariff deal coming 'soon' at Michigan border rally
Article:
WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump at a Sunday political rally predicted a trade dispute with Canada would be resolved "soon," without providing specifics.
At an event in Port Huron, Michigan, to boost Republican candidates ahead of the Nov 3 midterms, Trump and other speakers reiterated his oft-expressed position that higher tariffs on Canadian goods are needed because Canada "has been ripping off" the US in trade.
"I had to do it," Trump told the Michigan crowd. "We'll have that settled pretty soon. They're willing to give us anything at this moment."
The office of Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Trump won in Michigan's border region that includes Port Huron in the 2024 presidential election with more than 66 per cent of the vote, but the local economy has felt the impacts of the US-Canada tariff standoff, including the Detroit-based US auto industry.
Republican Congressman Mike Rogers, who is running in a tight race against Democratic rival Abdul El-Sayed, has tried to ​distance himself from the president's tariff policy on the auto sector.
Rogers on Sunday hailed Trump's tariffs for securing manufacturing investments ​for Michigan by ⁠Chevrolet and Detroit Diesel, but said "the automobile portion of these Canadian tariffs worries me a little bit."
"There's some good and there's some things we have to work on," he told "Meet the Press."

Title: US helped Gulf nations ship 1.5 billion barrels through Hormuz
Article:
RIYADH: US Central Command on Sunday said it helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via the Strait of Hormuz since summer, bypassing an Iranian blockade.
"U.S. forces reach the milestone of assisting Gulf partners in exporting more than 1.5 billion barrels of crude oil since summer," CENTCOM said in a statement posted on X.
"More than 3,000 commercial vessels have successfully transited the Strait of Hormuz with support from CENTCOM forces over the last six months," it added, stating that "over 95% of ships navigating the Strait of Hormuz have sailed through safely."
"Today, primary transit routes in the Strait of Hormuz remain free and clear of Iranian sea mines thanks to incredible efforts by our people," said CENTCOM chief admiral Brad Cooper, who was visiting US troops in Hormuz.
Iran has seized control over the vital waterway since the Middle East war erupted with US-Israeli strikes on the Islamic republic on Feb 28.
It has demanded permission for ships to transit the strait, through which a fifth of global oil exports normally pass.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said this month that Iran has "lost complete control" of the Strait of Hormuz, claiming that Teheran's economy was "in total and complete freefall."
"The Straits of Hormuz are open. There's almost as much oil flowing out now as there was before this conflict began. So they've lost complete control of the Straits," he said.
According to data from the maritime tracking firm Kpler, crude oil exports reached pre-war levels in September, with at least 16.5 million barrels leaving the region excluding Iran.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia makes progress in graft fight
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has completed 41 of the 60 sub-strategies under the National Anti-Corruption Strategy (NACS) 2024-2028, marking progress in efforts to strengthen governance and combat corruption.
Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) National Governance Planning Division Senior Director Datuk Idris Zaharudin said the achievement reflected the government's efforts to translate policy commitments into concrete action across ministries and agencies.
Launched in May 2024 by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, NACS provides a comprehensive framework to strengthen governance, integrity and accountability through legislative reforms, institutional improvement, the integration of anti-corruption education into school and university curricula, and stronger private sector accountability through corporate integrity programmes.
Speaking to the New Straits Times, Idris said the strategy was not merely a continuation of the previous anti-corruption plan, but an adoption of a more structured, phased and measurable approach to implementation.
"NACS was developed as a comprehensive strategic framework integrating legislative reforms, system enhancements, educational empowerment and collective involvement from the private sector and civil society," he said.
Among its key achievements are the enactment of the Border Control and Protection Agency Act 2025, the Government Procurement Act 2025 and the Parliamentary Services Act 2025.
NACS has also driven amendments to the Immigration Act 2025 and the Whistleblower Protection Act 2025, alongside the implementation of job rotation policies and the Demerit Performance Evaluation (DEEP) system.
Other measures include guidelines clarifying the roles and responsibilities of National Audit Department officers stationed in internal audit units at ministries, government departments, agencies and state secretariats.
Idris said NACS should not be treated as a static policy document, as governance challenges and institutional reforms need to evolve.
"More importantly, NACS is not viewed as a static policy document. It is a living document that evolves alongside current challenges and dynamic institutional reform needs," he said.
He said a key focus was ensuring that progress could be monitored systematically through two digital dashboards developed by the division and hosted on MACC servers.
"The r-NACS dashboard serves as an internal quarterly performance-monitoring tool between the NACS Secretariat and lead agencies, while the d-NACS dashboard provides public access to implementation information, including completed sub-strategies and key outputs by agency," he said.
Idris said the data-driven approach would strengthen accountability among implementing agencies besides allowing problems to be identified and addressed more quickly.
He added that the main challenge was ensuring reforms were implemented effectively at operational and grassroots levels.
[[nid:1563547]]
"The primary challenge now lies not at the strategy formulation stage, but in the capability to execute it effectively and comprehensively at the grassroots level," he said.
The reforms extend beyond enforcement, with education identified as a core component in building a long-term culture of integrity.
Integrity and anti-corruption modules have been incorporated into higher-learning institutions, alongside efforts to strengthen integrity-related content in primary and secondary school curricula.
Idris described education as a long-term investment in developing a generation capable of strengthening the country's institutions and leadership.
"Education is no longer considered a supporting component, but a core strategy in building a sustainable anti-corruption ecosystem," he said.
The strategy also emphasises the role of the private sector, particularly in government procurement, where public and corporate interests intersect.
Companies participating in public procurement are required to declare their beneficiary owners, while those bidding for government construction contracts worth more than RM100 million are subject to measures promoting the MS ISO 37001 Anti-Bribery Management Systems (ABMS) certification.
Tax incentives for companies obtaining ISO 37001 ABMS accreditation are also among measures aimed at encouraging stronger corporate anti-corruption practices, complementing corporate liability provisions under Section 17A of the MACC Act 2009.
Meanwhile, Malaysia aims to rank among the top 25 countries in the Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI) by 2030.
A special CPI task force has been established to identify gaps and formulate strategic interventions in enforcement, public fund management, business competitiveness, investment risks and legislative reform.
Idris said the anti-corruption agenda required sustained participation across the public sector, corporate world and civil society.
"The true effectiveness of NACS will not only be measured by the number of sub-strategies completed, but by the extent to which systemic change can be felt by the public through services that are more transparent, efficient and fair," he said.
With 41 sub-strategies completed, the next phase will focus on sustaining implementation, strengthening coordination and ensuring reforms translate into lasting institutional change.
NACS succeeds the National Anti-Corruption Plan (NACP) 2019-2023 and aims to position Malaysia as a corrupt-free and prosperous nation.
It comprises 60 sub-strategies overseen by 20 government ministries, departments and agencies, including MACC and the National Audit Department.

Title: Malaysia's 'green' test: Billions pledged, too few bankable
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Southeast Asian countries, including Malaysia, have announced hundreds of billions of dollars in green investments.
The real test is turning these commitments into projects on the ground.
For Malaysia, closing the gap between ambition and execution is crucial to boosting industrial competitiveness and attracting investment.
Delays, infrastructure bottlenecks and financing constraints risk slowing the energy transition.
Maybank group chief sustainability officer Datuk Shahril Azuar Jimin said the biggest hurdle was no longer a shortage of capital or climate commitments, but a lack of bankable projects capable of delivering measurable emissions reductions
"The money has always been there but what remains scarce is the number of bankable projects available," he told Business Times.
The gap between climate ambitions and actual investment is evident globally.
CDP's "From Plans to Capital" report found that 72 per cent of nearly 12,000 companies reporting through the platform had initiatives to reduce emissions, but only 11 per cent disclosed capital expenditure aligned with their transition strategies
About US$540 billion in green capital expenditure has been announced across Southeast Asia's power and electric vehicle value chains through 2030. However, only around US$315 billion is on a credible path to deployment, Shahril said.
The problem extends beyond financing.
Regulatory uncertainty, permitting delays, grid connection constraints and unclear power purchase agreements have undermined project viability despite investor interest.
Bain's 2026 report on Southeast Asia's green economy found that 50 to 60 per cent of renewable energy projects in Vietnam, Thailand and Indonesia were cancelled between 2021 and 2025, Shahril said.
The findings highlight barriers beyond the availability of capital.
The challenge is particularly pressing as Malaysia pursues its National Energy Transition Roadmap, which aims for renewable energy to account for 35 per cent of installed electricity-generation capacity by 2030 and 70 per cent by 2050.
For Shahril, the priority is to ensure that businesses, financiers and policymakers can translate those targets into viable projects, the infrastructure needed to support them and measurable results.
FROM AMBITION TO BANKABILITY
A credible transition plan must go beyond a company's pledge to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050.
It needs to establish a baseline for current emissions, set interim reduction targets, identify the required investments and demonstrate how they will be funded.
He said banks and investors needed to know whether a company's targets were achievable and adequately funded.
Shahril identified five essential elements: a reliable emissions baseline; a defined pathway with interim milestones; a capital expenditure plan linked to expected returns; alignment with recognised sustainability standards; and strong governance, accountability and regular reporting.
The Joint Committee on Climate Change has agreed to adopt the Asean Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance as the basis for Malaysia's taxonomy, Shahril said.
Independent assessments can further strengthen investor confidence by validating a project's environmental credentials and giving lenders a clearer basis for evaluating its risks.
Maybank Investment Bank Bhd, for instance, acted as sustainability framework adviser in developing Tenaga Nasional Bhd's Transition Finance Framework. The framework received a second-party opinion from Morningstar Sustainalytics and referenced the Asean Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance Version 2 and the Asean Transition Finance Guidance
Malakoff Corporation Bhd's Sustainable Finance Framework also received a 'Gold' Impact Assessment and a second-party opinion from MARC Ratings Bhd.
Such assessments translate broad climate ambitions into defined criteria that investors and credit committees can evaluate.
Shahril said the assessments also help distinguish companies backing their climate targets with actual investment from those making long-term pledges without corresponding near-term spending.
FINANCING THE TRANSITION, NOT JUST GREEN PROJECTS
A further challenge is decarbonising industries that cannot immediately abandon conventional energy sources.
Financing only businesses that are already green would leave some of the most difficult emissions reductions unaddressed, particularly in emerging economies where industrial activity and energy security remain critical.
Companies unable to switch technologies overnight need credible transition plans.  These should demonstrate measurable improvements in emissions intensity, avoid locking in high-carbon assets indefinitely and allow for deeper decarbonisation as technology and infrastructure mature.
Shahril said two financing transactions illustrate how this can work.
Malakoff's RM450 million SRI Sukuk Murabahah financed solar and hydropower projects, as well as identify the eligible project, which was assessed against the Asean Taxonomy's Amber Tier 2 lifecycle emissions thresholds.
The classification recognises a transitional role for high-efficiency gas while taking account of emissions criteria and energy security.
In Singapore, Maybank, DBS and OCBC jointly extended a S$500 million transition loan to YTL PowerSeraya.
The financing supports a 600-megawatt hydrogen-ready combined-cycle gas turbine (CCGT) power plant.
Shahril said it was the first transition finance deal aligned with the Singapore-Asia Taxonomy.
The H-class turbine is estimated to cut carbon dioxide emissions intensity by about 10 per cent compared with older F-class technology.
It can co-fire up to 50 per cent hydrogen at launch and could eventually be retrofitted to run fully on hydrogen as supply develops.
The project is targeted for completion by the end of 2027.
When commercially viable hydrogen supplies become available, co-firing 30 per cent hydrogen could reduce emissions intensity by a further 12 per cent, he said.
These targets give investors measurable benchmarks for assessing environmental performance and progress against the project's transition pathway.
However, lenders must also account for risks such as delays in hydrogen supply and supporting infrastructure.
Transition finance therefore requires the same rigour as conventional lending, with clear eligibility criteria, quantifiable performance indicators and contingency plans.
The quality of transition data is also increasingly influencing capital allocation.
Indeed, CDP's Corporate Health Check 2026 reported that financial institutions managing US$145 trillion in assets use transition-plan data in their due diligence.
Companies achieving CDP's leadership level also identified a combined US$218 billion in environmental opportunities.
The message for businesses is that credible data and measurable outcomes are becoming central to attracting capital, rather than optional additions to sustainability disclosures.
THE RISING COST OF NOT TRANSITIONING
For companies concerned about the upfront costs of decarbonisation, the economic risks of inaction are becoming harder to ignore.
The International Energy Agency estimates that Southeast Asia's fossil fuel import bill could rise from just over US$80 billion in 2024 to around US$245 billion by 2035 without structural changes.
Delivering on announced pledges could reduce that projected bill by roughly half, Shahril said.
The region's reliance on imported fuels exposes businesses and economies to price volatility, geopolitical disruption and higher energy costs.
Coal accounts for about half of Southeast Asia's electricity generation.
Shahril said regional coal demand had grown by about eight per cent annually. Coal's share of the energy mix rose from 20 per cent in 2015 to 30 per cent in 2026.
For Malaysia, the energy transition is also becoming a factor in attracting investment in data centres, advanced manufacturing and other electricity-intensive industries.
Peak electricity demand is projected to rise from 21.3 gigawatts in 2026 to 33.5 gigawatts by 2035, according to the Energy Transition and Water Transformation Ministry.
Data centres could account for about a third of electricity consumption by 2035, compared with around seven per cent today, Shahril said.
Meanwhile, 90 per cent of data centre operators surveyed in Asean identified grid-connection delays as a major constraint, with many willing to pay a premium for a guaranteed connection date.
"These companies are then choosing locations based on how quickly they can get reliable, increasingly green power.
"For Malaysia, the energy transition is therefore an economic policy. It can shape where companies invest and how industries compete."
MAKING THE TRANSITION COMMERCIALLY VIABLE
Businesses do not necessarily need to begin with their most expensive decarbonisation investments.
A phased approach can prioritise projects with relatively quick payback periods, including energy-efficiency improvements, rooftop solar and battery storage to reduce peak-demand charges.
The Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme also provides companies with a route to secure renewable electricity without developing generation assets themselves.
Matching long-term investments with appropriately structured financing can help spread upfront costs and improve project economics.
Technology selection is equally important, Shahril said, as not every emerging solution will deliver the expected commercial or environmental returns.
Companies must assess technology maturity, cost, performance and scalability before committing capital.
Malaysia's own programmes also demonstrate how transition investment can generate domestic economic benefits.
The 2026 Feed-in Tariff round is expected to catalyse RM4.3 billion in investment, create 7,738 jobs and generate about RM617 million in demand for locally manufactured equipment, he said.
These benefits strengthen the case for treating the energy transition as an industrial development strategy that can support local supply chains and employment, rather than solely as an environmental obligation.
BRING BANKS IN BEFORE PROJECTS ARE DESIGNED
Earlier engagement between businesses and financial institutions is another important factor in turning projects into bankable investments.
"It is incredibly critical, yet still underused. In fact, it is one of the biggest factors in whether a plan can reach financing at all," Shahril said.
When banks are approached only after a project has been designed, its financing structure may not adequately address technical assumptions, environmental requirements or risks.
Engaging lenders earlier allows companies to incorporate taxonomy criteria, disclosure requirements and investor expectations before key decisions are finalised.
Tenaga Nasional's Transition Finance Framework, developed with Maybank Investment Banking Group, enables the utility to issue green, sustainability and transition-labelled instruments, including SRI sukuk.
The framework comes as TNB plans to invest RM43 billion in strengthening the grid between 2025 and 2027, supporting the infrastructure needed to accommodate Malaysia's changing energy mix.
Shahril said YTL PowerSeraya engaged its financing banks early and throughout the process.
This allowed the CCGT's technical design, emissions performance and taxonomy alignment to be considered in the credit assessment from the outset.
The JC3 Climate Finance Innovation Lab reflects a similar approach.
It has onboarded 30 projects with combined funding requirements exceeding RM4 billion, while a second cohort of 22 projects is seeking RM1.73 billion, he said.
"Getting projects ready for financing early and ensuring they receive viability support are what make them bankable and, I think, really move the needle," Shahril said.
However, financing readiness must also account for infrastructure constraints that could undermine a project's financial assumptions.
Shahril said Peninsular Malaysia's grid could accommodate around six gigawatts of additional renewable capacity, compared with about 4.5 gigawatts already installed.
Studies suggest each additional 1,000 megawatts of renewable capacity may require around 500 megawatts of storage.
Projects that overlook grid access, connection capacity, storage requirements or delivery timelines risk being less viable than their initial financial projections suggest.
Coordination between utilities, regulators, developers and financiers is therefore essential to ensure that project design, infrastructure investment and financing move in tandem.
EXECUTION IS THE NEXT TEST
Malaysia has made progress in establishing its energy transition framework.
Its installed renewable energy capacity has reached 32 per cent, exceeding the 31 per cent target for 2025, Shahril said.
The National Energy Transition Roadmap and the Energy Transition and Water Transformation Ministry's Strategic Plan for 2026–2030 provide further direction.
The Large Scale Solar 6 programme is expected to attract about RM6 billion in private investment for two gigawatts of solar capacity.
But policy ambition alone will not close the financing gap.
He said disciplined execution was now essential, with each stakeholder having a different role to play.
Policymakers, for example, could make the project pipeline more visible and predictable.
Policymakers must provide predictable tender schedules, bankable power purchase agreements and reliable grid connection timelines.
Businesses, meanwhile, need credible investment plans backed by emissions data, realistic milestones and clear accountability.
Banks must go beyond lending to help structure transactions, assess transition risks and support projects with credible long-term potential, he said.
Under its ROAR30 strategy, Maybank aims to mobilise RM300 billion in sustainable finance between 2026 and 2030.
Shahril warned that Southeast Asia had an estimated 24 to 36 months to demonstrate that announced capital could be converted into delivered projects, with around US$80 billion in investment at stake.
He said no single institution could close the gap alone and called for coordinated action to turn investment commitments into delivered projects.

Title: Vista sees stronger private aviation demand in Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Vista's flight traffic in Malaysia rose 18 per cent year-on-year in the first half of 2026, higher than the 14 per cent growth recorded across Asia Pacific.
Vista chief business officer Youssef Mouallem said the growth is supported by industrial activity in Malaysia and demand from business travellers seeking greater flexibility and shorter travel time.
"We see a big part of the industrial attraction in Malaysia. Business aviation has always been a tool for enabling business and we're seeing it come into play with that," he told Business Times in an exclusive interview recently.
Mouallem said private aviation demand in Malaysia is growing faster than the wider Asia Pacific market and he expects the trend to continue in the second half of the year.
"Malaysia is growing ahead of the region. That's year-on-year. We've seen an accelerating trend. So, expect this to continue and probably even accelerate further in the second half (of the year)," he added.
Vista is a global business aviation group operating VistaJet, which provides private jet services through its fleet and membership programmes, and XO, which offers on-demand access to about 2,000 vetted aircraft worldwide.
Malaysia is Vistajet's first market in Southeast Asia, having entered into the country in 2008 before expanding across the region.
Mouallem said that Southeast Asia remains an important market for Vista and serves as a link to Oceania.
"The growth rates are higher than our global average, so it's a growth market for us, and we continue to invest in that," he added.
Mouallem said XO provides access to a global marketplace of about 2,000 vetted aircraft, allowing customers to check aircraft availability and pricing before booking.
Elsewhere in Southeast Asia, Vista also recorded strong traffic growth in several markets in the first half of 2026.
Singapore's flight traffic rose 58 per cent year-on-year, while flight hours increased 51 per cent.
Indonesia recorded 27 per cent growth, while Vietnam and the Philippines posted an increase of 64 per cent and 62 per cent, respectively.
Mouallem said Vista is also seeing younger customers entering private aviation, particularly in Asia.
About 47 per cent of Vista's new flyers in 2025 are below 45 years old.
"These are entrepreneurs. These are tech millionaires. These are AI and crypto players. There's a lot of that wealth coming into the industry," Mouallem said, adding that these customers are looking for flexibility, quicker access to aircraft and the ability to book closer to their travel date.
Vista's average booking lead time has fallen from about 14 days to nine days, he said.
"They want the flexibility. They don't want to commit early and they want the access," he added.
Another trend that Vista is seeing in Southeast Asia is the demand for regional and long-range business jets.
Mouallem said the Bombardier Challenger 600 aircraft remains in demand for regional flying, while longer-haul demand includes the large-cabin Bombardier Global 6000 and the Global 7500 aircraft.
Vista is also upgrading its Global 7500 fleet to Global 8000.
"We've completed 11 out of our fleet of 18, and the other seven will be done before the end of the year," Mouallem said.
On fuel costs, he said higher jet fuel prices have not had a significant impact on Vista's flying demand.
"I wouldn't say it's a concern. It's a dynamic that you have to deal with. We haven't seen a real impact on the flying trend or on demand," he added.
Mouallem also said further growth in Asia's private aviation market depends on improvements across the wider business aviation ecosystem, including service levels, governance and digitalisation.
"For the overall industry to thrive, you need the whole ecosystem to move forward. We'd expect all of the other players to really improve service levels, safety, and governance. There's a lot of grey market or parallel brokering, so that's something that does not necessarily help the industry."
"It allows access but it does not allow the industry to develop as a whole," he said, adding that greater digitalisation is needed across services such as flight planning, fixed-base operators (FBOs), onboard servicing and catering to provide a more integrated experience for customers.

Title: Share upside as plantation stocks draw attention on earnings, dividends
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Ta Ann Holdings Bhd has emerged as the most attractive plantation stock in terms of potential share-price gains, with a target price of RM8.55 implying a 50.5 per cent upside, as improving production, earnings prospects and dividend yields underpin investment interest in the sector.
Public Investment Bank (PublicInvest) has named Ta Ann, Genting Plantations Bhd, SD Guthrie Bhd and Sarawak Plantation Bhd as "Outperform" picks, while maintaining "Neutral" calls on IOI Corp Bhd and Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd (KLK).
Ta Ann's target price of RM8.55 compares with its market price of RM5.68 (Oct 20), giving it the highest potential upside among the six plantation companies assessed.
SD Guthrie follows with a target price of RM7.81, representing a 36.5 per cent upside from RM5.72 (Oct 20), while Genting Plantations has a target price of RM6.84, implying a 34.1 per cent gain from RM5.10 (Oct 20), the firm said in a recent note.
It said Sarawak Plantation offers a potential upside of 27.9 per cent, with a target price of RM5.59 against its price of RM4.37 (Oct 20).
Among the larger plantation counters, KLK has a target price of RM23.86, suggesting an 18.4 per cent upside from RM20.16 (Oct 20), while IOI Corp has a target price of RM5.06, representing a 12.4 per cent gain from RM4.50 (Oct 20).
The preference for selected plantation stocks comes as investors weigh earnings growth and dividend income against commodity-price volatility, production costs and changing export dynamics.
Based on financial forecasts, PublicInvest analyst Chong Hoe Leong said Ta Ann offers the highest projected dividend yield among the six companies at 8.8 per cent for both financial years 2026 and 2027. Sarawak Plantation follows at 6.9 per cent, while Genting Plantations offers 5.8 per cent.
Ta Ann's appeal is further supported by its earnings outlook. Its earnings per share (EPS) are forecast to rise from 63.3 sen in 2026 to 66.1 sen in 2027, while its forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio is expected to decline from nine times to 8.6 times.
Sarawak Plantation is also expected to deliver earnings growth, with EPS projected to increase from 43.1 sen in 2026 to 46.6 sen in 2027. Its forward P/E ratio is forecast to ease from 10.1 times to 9.4 times, alongside a projected dividend yield of 6.9 per cent.
Its return on equity (ROE) is expected to improve from 13.9 per cent in 2026 to 14.3 per cent in 2027, placing it among the stronger performers in the group.
Genting Plantations, meanwhile, is forecast to record EPS of 46.9 sen in 2026 and 47.1 sen in 2027, with its forward P/E ratio remaining relatively stable at 10.9 times and 10.8 times, respectively.
The outlook is less straightforward for SD Guthrie, despite its substantial implied share-price upside. Its EPS is projected to decline from 42.7 sen in 2026 to 39 sen in 2027, representing a fall of 8.6 per cent, while its forward P/E ratio is expected to rise from 13.4 times to 14.7 times. Its dividend yield is also forecast to moderate from 3.8 per cent to 3.5 per cent.
For IOI Corp, EPS is expected to rise from 25.1 sen in 2026 to 26.2 sen in 2027, while its forward P/E ratio declines from 17.9 times to 17.2 times. Its dividend yield is projected to edge up from 2.8 per cent to 2.9 per cent.
KLK is similarly expected to post moderate earnings growth, with EPS rising from RM1.162 to RM1.204 over the same period. Its forward P/E ratio is forecast to ease from 17.3 times to 16.7 times, while its dividend yield remains at 3 per cent.
Ta Ann also leads the group in projected ROE, at 15.6 per cent in 2026 and 15.3 per cent in 2027, followed by Sarawak Plantation at 13.9 per cent and 14.3 per cent, respectively.
The valuations suggest that Ta Ann and Sarawak Plantation offer a combination of income and earnings growth, while the target-price upside at SD Guthrie and Genting Plantations may appeal to investors seeking capital appreciation.
However, target prices are estimates rather than guaranteed returns, and the sector's performance will remain sensitive to crude palm oil prices, fresh fruit bunch production, operating costs and export competitiveness.

Title: Zelenskyy: US-Ukraine-Russia meeting to take place in November
Article:
KYIV: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Sunday said that a trilateral meeting between Kyiv, Washington and Moscow would take place in November aiming to restart stalled peace talks.
"We are ready to talk. If it's a territorial issue, it must be addressed at a leadership level. Other issues fall within the remit of the technical groups. All this can therefore be discussed in November," Zelenskyy said in an interview with Ukrainian television.
On Friday Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said that a trilateral meeting was planned to take place in the United Arab Emirates in November.
The announcements came amid intensified diplomatic efforts by US President Donald Trump's administration.
His envoy Steve Witkoff met on Tuesday with Zelenskyy and European leaders in Oslo, before meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday.
Following the meetings, both Kyiv and Moscow voiced their readiness to resume direct talks mediated by Washington.--AFP

Title: Malaysia's missing economic map
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia measures what its states produce. It does not yet adequately measure what they produce together.
We know the size of each state economy, its industries, household incomes and international trade. Less visible are the goods, services, workers, capital and knowledge crossing state boundaries before final output reaches the market.
This gap affects how Malaysia understands regional inequality, designs infrastructure and distributes development expenditure. State GDP identifies where value is created. It cannot, alone, explain how that value moves through the federation or reaches households.
Malaysia already publishes national input-output accounts and has valuable regional research. It needs a regularly updated, publicly accessible official framework measuring production flows between individual states.
States Apart, Factories Together
Penang and Kedah are separate jurisdictions but increasingly connected production locations. Bayan Lepas, Perai, Batu Kawan and Kulim draw upon overlapping suppliers, skills, logistics and multinational networks.
Penang contributes accumulated industrial capabilities. Kulim offers additional land, utilities and manufacturing capacity. Firms can expand while retaining access to Penang's ecosystem. This is a regional division of productive functions.
The Northern Corridor Implementation Authority has a statutory mandate to coordinate development across Penang, Kedah, Perlis and Perak. Better interstate production accounts would strengthen its decisions on infrastructure, supplier development and investment, helping establish what each state contributes and captures.
Penang accounted for 38.1 per cent of Malaysian exports in 2025. That demonstrates international exposure, without revealing purchases from Kedah or where the resulting wages and profits accrue.
Malaysia measures the corridor's transactions with the world more readily than the domestic relationships making them possible.
Industrial expansion also needs to deliver technological upgrading. More factories do not automatically create Malaysian intellectual property or stronger domestic ownership. The test is whether supplier capabilities deepen, firms enter higher-value activities and workers' incomes rise.
Output Is Not Household Prosperity
Sabah and Sarawak expose different weaknesses in the same statistical picture.
Sabah's economy grew by 5.1 per cent in 2025, yet manufacturing contributed only 7.2 per cent of state GDP, compared with Sarawak's 24.9 per cent and Penang's 47.3 per cent. Its challenge concerns the structure beneath growth.
When commodities leave Sabah for processing elsewhere, potential gains extend beyond factory margins. Testing, engineering, branding and supplier relationships accumulate where production occurs. Rebuilding those capabilities later is difficult.
Sabah needs commercially viable downstream production around palm oil, fisheries and food processing. Incentives should reward operating facilities, skilled jobs, local purchases and products delivered.
Sarawak's GDP per capita exceeded the national average in 2024. Yet its mean monthly household income was RM6,947, below Malaysia's RM9,155 that year. Annual output per person and monthly income per household are not directly comparable. The two comparisons nevertheless warrant investigating how production translates into residents' welfare.
They do not establish that profits are leaving Sarawak. Ownership, labour compensation, household composition and the destination of operating surpluses remain matters for investigation.
Sarawak's Global Supply Chain and Sourcing Programme connects anchor investors with local suppliers. Its success should be measured through procurement, contracts, technology transfer, wages and projects reaching commercial production. Durable economic relationships are the objective.
Production networks also explain vulnerability. Diesel connects plantations, harvesting crews, mills, ports and exports. Higher costs or shortages propagate through these chains, with distance and infrastructure shaping the regional burden.
Count Connections, Not Just Allocations
Budget 2027 supports initiatives including Kulim Hi-Tech Park, Sibu Special Economic Zone negotiations, Sabah's electricity projects and RM3.3 billion for roads in Sabah and Sarawak. Alongside the Perak–Penang bulk-water agreement, these form elements of a national production architecture.
Water security supports Penang's industry. Reliable electricity affects Sabah's capacity to industrialise. Roads can lower the cost of building Borneo supply chains. Their value extends beyond the jurisdiction where expenditure occurs.
Federal spending should therefore be judged by the connections it enables and the distribution of benefits, alongside allocations received.
The six less-developed states allocated RM21.26 billion in federal development expenditure cannot be treated as one category. Kedah needs deeper participation in advanced manufacturing networks; Sabah needs downstream capacity and reliable infrastructure; Sarawak needs stronger conversion of production into household prosperity.
Malaysia's New Incentive Framework shifts attention towards outcomes. Monitoring should include where suppliers, workers and research activities are located and whether investment strengthens domestic firms across state boundaries. Does a Penang project purchase inputs from Kedah? Does a Sarawak investment create local supplier contracts and skilled employment for resident workers?
Existing research offers a foundation. A January 2026 study by Pang Chun Sian and Mohd Khairul Hisyam Hassan constructs a 2015 interregional input-output table covering Sabah, Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia, estimating flows across 30 sectors. This work should be extended and institutionalised. However, treating the peninsula as one region cannot reveal production relationships between its individual states.
The Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) could build linked state and interregional accounts using administrative records and targeted surveys. A table linking states would show which industries buy from which locations, making interdependence visible. Estimates should be balanced, validated and published with uncertainty ranges. Policymakers need reliable answers to specific questions while more comprehensive accounts develop.
Three pilots would be useful: Penang–Kedah semiconductor dependence, Sabah's downstream-processing deficit and Sarawak's energy-transition exposure. Each should identify essential purchases by origin and destination, freight flows, supplier locations, commuting patterns and employment links.
Linking production accounts to social accounting matrices would help trace payments to workers, owners and households. Ownership, wage and income data could distinguish each state's contribution to production from the benefits retained by residents and test whether growth is narrowing regional disparities.
Comparable benefit-cost analysis should guide interstate electricity, water, transport and digital infrastructure. It must identify who finances shared assets, who benefits and where investment follows. Energy-transition gains and losses may occur in different states and affect different workers.
The federalism question concerns how states produce together and whether the gains are shared.
Malaysia already finances interstate production architecture. Its accounting framework should make those connections and their distributional consequences clearer.
Regional policy must move from counting allocations to measuring connections, and from celebrating output to examining household prosperity.
Malaysia's economic map is not empty. It is incomplete. The task is to draw the missing lines.
===================
Economist Samirul Ariff Othman is an international relations analyst and a senior consultant with Global Asia Consulting (GAC). Samirul has a background as a senior researcher at the Malaysian Institute of Economic Research. The viewpoints articulated are solely those of the author.

Title: Building costs soar, but Mah Sing limits increase to 10pc
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Rising building material prices are putting pressure on property developers to protect profit margins without pricing homebuyers out of the market, as industry players grapple with reported increases of 20 per cent to 30 per cent in selected construction inputs.
However, the impact on overall project costs varies depending on the materials used, their contribution to total construction expenses and developers' ability to negotiate competitive procurement terms, according to Mah Sing Group Bhd founder and group managing director Tan Sri Leong Hoy Kum.
Leong said the group's overall construction costs had increased by an estimated 5.0 per cent to 10 per cent, significantly below the reported price hikes for certain building materials.
He attributed this to the group's emphasis on value engineering, economies of scale and long-standing supplier relationships, which help it manage expenses while maintaining its product positioning.
The approach is particularly important as Mah Sing continues to focus on homes priced between RM300,000 and RM700,000, with selected offerings extending to RM800,000, catering to buyers seeking affordability without compromising on quality.
Leong said the reported 20 per cent to 30 per cent increase in building material prices over the past year was a general industry estimate and did not reflect the group's own experience.
"Some materials may have experienced significant price hikes, but their actual contribution to total construction costs could be relatively small," he told Business Times on the sidelines of the opening of the M Mira sales gallery in Setapak, recently.
He said a sharp increase in the price of an individual material did not necessarily translate into a comparable rise in a project's overall construction budget, as the impact depended on its share of total costs.
Materials such as cement, steel and sand form part of the construction cost structure, but their respective contributions vary across projects.
Materials with a relatively small cost base, for instance, could record steep percentage increases without significantly changing the overall construction bill, Leong said.
To manage these pressures, Mah Sing incorporates value engineering from the initial design stage, enabling its teams to optimise layouts, specifications and construction methods while maintaining the intended product quality.
"We practise value engineering from day one, ensuring that our designs are planned efficiently to manage costs," he said.
The group also draws on its established supplier network and long-standing relationships to secure competitive terms.
As a large customer, Mah Sing benefits from purchasing scale and its reputation as a reliable payer, strengthening its bargaining position with suppliers, Leong said.
He added that several departments worked together to monitor expenses and maintain tight control over project budgets, allowing the group to identify potential cost pressures early and manage them throughout the development process.
The distinction between individual material price movements and overall construction costs is increasingly important for developers, particularly those targeting first-time homebuyers and middle-income households, where affordability remains a key consideration.
According to the Real Estate and Housing Developers' Association (Rehda) Malaysia, construction costs rose by an average of 13 per cent in the first half of 2026.
Rehda president Datuk Zaini Yusoff said earthworks and infrastructure costs had increased by between 20 per cent and 30 per cent, while normal building works recorded increases of 3.0 per cent to 5.0 per cent.
The divergent cost movements highlight the uneven pressure across different construction components, with developers having to contend with higher expenses in specific areas while managing overall project budgets.
Olive Tree Property Consultants founder and chief executive officer Samuel Tan said developers faced a difficult balancing act as higher construction costs threatened to erode margins, while passing the increases on to buyers risked weakening demand.
Developers must therefore manage both their cost structures and selling prices to keep projects commercially viable, he told Business Times when contacted.
For Mah Sing, Leong said maintaining cost discipline was central to preserving its position in the mass-market and mid-market residential segments.
He said the group's focus on homes priced between RM300,000 and RM700,000 reflects its strategy of catering to buyers seeking relatively affordable properties, while retaining flexibility to offer selected units priced up to RM800,000.
"The group's ability to contain construction cost increases below the reported industry material price movements could provide some buffer against cost volatility, although the extent of the benefit will depend on future material prices, labour costs and the requirements of individual projects."
Looking ahead to 2027, Leong said Mah Sing would remain focused on its existing property development strategy, with cost management and affordability continuing to guide its growth plans amid an evolving construction cost environment.

Title: 'Marine has to win': Le Pen supporters fear France is in decline
Article:
ORLÉANS, France: Wrapped in the French tricolour, Loic Le Tourneau was among thousands of supporters who flocked on Sunday to see far-right leader Marine Le Pen officially launch her presidential campaign.
Outside the arena in the city of Orleans, fans milled about, tucking into hot dogs and French fries and snapping up Le Pen-branded T-shirts and scarves before heading inside.
But behind the festive atmosphere lay deep-seated anxieties about France's future among the roughly 8,500 people who turned out to hear the leader of the nationalist, anti-immigration party.
Le Tourneau, who travelled nearly an hour to attend the rally, said he was increasingly worried about insecurity in France – even though he said he had not experienced it firsthand in the countryside where he lives.
"I'm afraid because things have been deteriorating enormously for about ten years now," the 25-year-old told AFP.
"I'm worried things will keep getting worse if the National Rally doesn't come to power next year."
Polls show Le Pen – who has already made three unsuccessful presidential bids – is the frontrunner in the race to succeed centrist President Emmanuel Macron in next year's election.
But critics accuse her Eurosceptic party of remaining fundamentally racist despite her efforts to distance it from the legacy of her father, who co-founded what was then called the National Front and was convicted over racist and antisemitic remarks.
Her campaign launch came after weeks of unrest across France, where largely peaceful mass demonstrations have at times descended into violence and looting not seen in years.
Accusing Macron's centrist government of being soft on violent protesters, Le Pen vowed on Sunday to "restore the rule of law."
For Jacques Olivier, 65, a longtime supporter of the National Front then the National Rally, the stakes could hardly be higher.
"Marine has to win, otherwise France will collapse," said Olivier, who came from the Paris region.
He blamed immigration in part for what he saw as rising crime and violence.
"When you open the borders to the entire world, you get some not very nice people coming into our country to take advantage of us and to loot," he said, calling for "radical change."
"We have nothing to lose and everything to gain," he added.
-'WE'RE GOING TO WIN'-
Le Pen is running for the top job after an appeals court earlier this year upheld a graft conviction against her, but shortened a ban on her holding public office.
The choice of Orleans was a symbolic one: Joan of Arc lifted an English siege there in 1429 before being burned at the stake two years later.
Le Pen invoked the Catholic warrior – revered by the far right as a symbol of national resistance – in her speech, recalling how she had freed the city from a "foreign threat."
Among those drawn to Le Pen's message was Marie, a 19-year-old supporter with two French flags poking out of her handbag, who wanted a tougher stance on immigration.
"Those who love France should stay, and those who don't should leave," she said, declining to give her surname.
She also believed Le Pen would put an end to the "appalling" violence that has marred recent protests.
"There wouldn't be any more violent demonstrations," she said.
Yet despite the bleak picture supporters painted of France's current situation, the mood inside the arena was one of optimism.
Throughout the evening, the crowd repeatedly erupted into chants of "We're going to win! We're going to win!"--AFP

Title: Eisenkot takes aim at Netanyahu as Israel heads to polls
Article:
TEL AVIV: Israeli election contender Gadi Eisenkot on Sunday vowed to unite the country as he held his final major rally before the vote, while Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu sought to tar his main rival as soft on Iran.
Netanyahu has campaigned heavily on his security credentials, but Eisenkot has cast him as unfit to lead and pledged a state commission of inquiry into the failings that led to Hamas's Oct 7, 2023 attack under the incumbent's watch.
Polls had showed Netanyahu and Eisenkot running neck and neck before a ban on new polling took effect in the three days before Tuesday's vote.
Speaking to an audience of hundreds on Sunday, Eisenkot pledged to heal divisions inside Israeli society after Netanyahu's divisive tenure, and voiced "a commitment to security and the economy."
"Our goal is not for one side to defeat the other. That is not our way," he said. "We will work to bring all Israelis together again – those who voted for us and those who did not."
A relative newcomer to politics – in contrast with Netanyahu and his 30 years on the scene – Eisenkot's pledge to unite Israelis has resonated with some voters, and for many the ex-army chief's plain-spokenness is part of his appeal.
"I feel that he's a rock for us... he's someone I can trust," Yael Shkedi, a 66-year-old jewellery maker, said at Eisenkot's rally.
"Amid all this chaos, what really matters to me is this feeling of someone who can somehow bring everyone together, almost like a father figure."
In his speech, Eisenkot said he would "always look you in the eye and tell the truth", and pledged to "take responsibility for both successes and failures."
He also appealed directly to wavering supporters of Netanyahu's Likud party, urging them to change course.
"Deep down, you too know that Israel cannot go on like this," he said. "Israel needs change."
Netanyahu's critics accuse him of putting his political survival above the greater good, and he is currently facing trial on corruption charges, which he denies.
Rally attendee Chen Sharon, an army reservist, said she wanted "people that I can count on" in office.
"We need someone that we can actually believe his values and what he represents to us," she said.
- 'A CATASTROPHE FOR ISRAEL' -
Over the course of the campaign Netanyahu has played to Israeli voters' opposition to the creation of a Palestinian state, and posters have been splashed across the country with the slogan "Either the Right or Palestine."
He has also touted the still-unresolved war that he launched against Iran alongside US President Donald Trump, who has endorsed him in the race.
Appearing after Eisenkot's rally on Channel 14, Netanyahu again suggested the ex-general and his allies "want to create a Palestinian state, a catastrophe for Israel."
"They will not destroy Iran's nuclear programme," he told a boisterous studio audience. "We've done 90 per cent of the work, 10 per cent remains. Who is going to do it? Eisenkot and the Muslim Brotherhood? No. Only I can do it."
Eisenkot has said he is opposed to a Palestinian state, but has vowed to crack down on extremist West Bank settlers who have attacked Palestinians with impunity.
Netanyahu on Sunday posted an AI-generated image of a mushroom cloud engulfing Tel Aviv, alongside text attributed to a right-wing political commentator calling Iran an existential threat and arguing that all the other issues discussed this election season were trivial in comparison.
In a post on X addressing Netanyahu on Saturday, Eisenkot accused the premier of playing up the Iran threat when it suited him politically.
"You have once again failed spectacularly and blatantly to achieve the war objectives you yourself set," he added.
Longtime opposition leader Yair Lapid, who has promised to join a coalition with Eisenkot, said Netanyahu had "lost his grip."
"Yesterday, Netanyahu announced that US security aid was over and that sanctions would crush our economy. This morning, he posted a video in which an atomic bomb lands on Tel Aviv," he said on X.
"This man has lost his grip. We absolutely must send him home."--AFP
