Title: Brazil braces for result of knife-edge election after voting chaos
Article:
RIO DE JANEIRO: Brazil braced Sunday for the results of a nail-biting election pitting leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva against right-wing senator Flavio Bolsonaro, after a last-minute order to extend polling by two hours generated chaos and confusion.
It is the final electoral battle for Lula, who turns 81 on Tuesday and is hoping to pull off a dramatic turnaround after coming in second to the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro in the first round of voting.
Final polls showed the two candidates neck-and-neck.
The counting of votes from Brazil's electronic machines restarted after a last-minute order from the Supreme Court to extend voting. Results are usually available in a few hours.
Lula had asked for the extension, claiming that buses had been pulled from circulation in Sao Paulo and key northeastern cities, a bastion of his support.
Flavio Bolsonaro also requested an extension in some parts of the country due to heavy rains.
Some polling stations had already closed, and tallies had begun streaming in when polling stations where ordered to stay open.
In a clarification, Supreme Court Justice Cristiano Zanin said the order only applied to "locations where polling stations have not yet been closed."
- 'WE ARE WATCHING' -
Sunday's runoff will determine whether Brazil remains one of Latin America's few leftist nations or joins a regional swing to the right championed by US President Donald Trump.
Lula, who is seeking a fourth non-consecutive term, has pitched himself as a bulwark against US interference and democratic backsliding.
Trump, an ally of Flavio Bolsonaro's father, simply said "we are watching, yeah," when asked about Brazil's election on Sunday.
The 45-year-old senator has vowed to crack down on crime and slash government spending, while handing Brazil to "the Lord Jesus Christ."
"The time has come for real change," he declared after voting in Rio de Janeiro.
"This is about renewal, enough of the same old thing," 67-year-old retiree Eduardo Viana told AFP, adding that Lula "says he governs for the poor...just look, people can't even go to the supermarket."
Bolsonaro presents himself as more moderate than his firebrand father, who is serving a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup after he lost in the 2022 elections.
After its first-round defeat, the left swung into action with massive rallies highlighting Jair Bolsonaro's chaotic handling of the Covid pandemic, devastation of the Amazon rainforest and cuts to public programs.
Deforestation of the world's largest rainforest has hit its lowest level in four decades under Lula.
Yet, as the El Nino weather phenomenon fuelled fires across the Amazon in recent weeks, and rains lashed the south, climate change barely featured in the campaign.
- LULA'S REVAMP -
Lula, revered for social welfare programs that lifted millions out of poverty, made a dramatic comeback to office in 2022 elections after a corruption scandal saw him jailed for over 18 months.
The charges, annulled on procedural grounds, have continued to haunt him.
In his third term he has overseen a drop in inflation and unemployment, and lifted millions out of hunger, but voters complain about the cost of living and a sense of insecurity.
After his first-round blow, Lula revamped his social media strategy and even bought his first cellphone.
A fierce social media battle drew in Meta, parent company of WhatsApp, Facebook and Instagram, which Lula's campaign accused of favoring his opponent with "algorithmic manipulation."
Meta denied this but acknowledged that some of Lula's campaign ads had been mistakenly deactivated due to technical errors.
The bitterly divisive campaign alienated many voters, including doorman Joao Inacio Oliveira, who told AFP he would make a last-minute decision at the polling station.
"I don't know who I'm going to vote for," said Oliveira, 72. "I don't have any hope in the governments that come and go in Brazil."--AFP

Title: 38,000 women to benefit from mammogram screening subsidies
Article:

THE National Population and Family Development Board has allocated RM9 million for mammogram screening subsidies, which will benefit 38,000 women.
Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said the allocation was part of the government's efforts to encourage more women to undergo early breast cancer screening.
She said the government hoped more women would take advantage of the initiative.
"Next year, 38,000 women will benefit from this subsidy, including an estimated 9,000 in Sarawak," she said after the launch of the state-level Breast Cancer Awareness Month 2026 celebrations at Padang Merdeka here yesterday.
Nancy encouraged women to register early to secure screening slots at the available facilities.
The board introduced the mammogram subsidy programme in 2007 to widen access to early breast cancer screening.
As of Sept 30, the programme had benefited 598,919 women nationwide.
"In Sarawak, 90,075 women had undergone screening, with 88 found to have cancer."
Nancy said mammogram screening facilities were available at several hospitals in Sarawak, including in Kuching, Sibu and Miri.
"Early screening is important as breast cancer is one of the most common cancers affecting women. Don't wait until you turn 40 to undergo screening," she added.

Title: Serbia's student movement ousts longtime leader in parliament poll
Article:
BELGRADE: Serbia's student-led movement declared victory in parliamentary elections Sunday ending 14 years in power for Aleksandar Vucic's right-wing populist party.
The victory in the snap vote comes after nearly two years of anti-government protests sparked by the 2024 collapse of a canopy at Novi Sad railway station that killed 16 people.
The disaster has been widely blamed on corruption and triggered some of Serbia's largest protests since the fall of strongman Slobodan Milosevic in 2000.
"Preliminary results show that students are convincingly leading in almost all polling stations," Radomir Saicic, a candidate for the Students' List, said in a speech at the movement's election HQ.
"Students won and with them also a hope that Serbia can be a country of justice, freedom and dignity."
Voters cast ballots in huge numbers on Sunday, with the country recording its highest parliamentary election turnout in more than three decades.
Vucic conceded defeat less than two hours after polls closed, triggering raucous scenes in the capital as supporters of the movement celebrated the defeat of a government they blamed for deep-rooted corruption.
"I feel incredible," student Mila Martic told AFP from the List's headquarters. "I feel as though I am finally living in a free country."
Thousands poured into the capital's streets to celebrate the victory, with passing cars honking, crowds chanting, and fireworks lighting up the skyline.
According to the country's election officials, nearly 65 per cent of its 6.4 million registered voters had cast their ballots by 6pm, two hours before polls closed.
The figure surpassed the 1993 parliamentary election, when just over 61 percent voted.
- 'DREAM HAS COME TRUE' -
During his speech to supporters, Vucic said preliminary figures suggested the student movement could win between 135 and 140 seats, handing it an outright majority in the 250-seat parliament.
The 56-year-old statesman, who has maintained close ties with Russia throughout his tenure, blamed foreign powers for the result.
"I want people to know, this was the validation of a revolution carried out with the direct support of various European countries and the US deep state, the one that is also against President Trump," he said.
For nearly two years, students have staged rallies and marched across the Balkan nation to reach voters directly and counter the media machine of Vucic's Serbian Progressive Party.
Their protests have drawn huge crowds, a final pre-election rally in Belgrade on Thursday attracting around 150,000 people, according to an independent protest monitor.
"A two-year-long dream has come true," Mirjana Nikolic, a candidate on the Students' List, said shortly after the win was announced.
- POLITICAL NOVICES -
Most of the student list's 250 candidates are experts from fields including academia and the arts with little political experience.
The movement has a broad platform, centred on a pledge to fight corruption.
It evolved from demands for a transparent investigation into the Novi Sad tragedy into calls for an early election.
Despite pushing back against the movement for almost two years, Vucic under mounting pressure, called the vote last month, citing "major turbulence on the domestic political scene."
The right-wing populist leader resigned the presidency to run for prime minister.
Domestic and international observers were monitoring the vote, with students mobilising large numbers of volunteers to oversee the process.--AFP

Title: Netanyahu warns Iran may try to disrupt election, says 'don't test us'
Article:
JERUSALEM: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said that Iran and its allies might try to disrupt Tuesday's Israeli elections, warning the Islamic republic against any hostile acts.
The remarks came as Israel's Channel 12 reported, citing unnamed sources, that there had been a confrontation between Netanyahu and army chief Eyal Zamir over an unspecified new directive in the war with Iran, which the premier denied.
Netanyahu has campaigned heavily on his security credentials, touting the war he launched against Iran in February alongside the United States and suggesting that he alone can see it through.
"We have intelligence signs that our enemies, Iran and its proxies, could challenge us with attacks in order to disrupt the elections," Netanyahu said in a video released by his office on Sunday.
"Don't test us. You will suffer disproportionate blows," he added, noting the military was ready for both defensive and offensive operations.
In its report on the purported confrontation between Netanyahu and Zamir, Channel 12 said the latter had "demanded an in-depth discussion before carrying out the directive he had received, as well as legal guarantees and the signatures of the political echelon."
It did not offer details of the directive, but cited sources saying there were concerns within the army that the war might be exploited for political gain.
In a television appearance later in the day, Netanyahu dismissed the report as "nothing but rubbish."
Opposition leader Yair Lapid referenced the report in a post on X, accusing Netanyahu of seeking to put off the vote.
"Tonight it was published that he wants to set off an escalation and a confrontation with Iran, just to postpone the elections," he said.
"This man has lost his grip. We absolutely must send him home."
Earlier on Sunday, the premier posted an AI-generated image of a mushroom cloud engulfing Tel Aviv, alongside text attributed to a right-wing political commentator calling Iran an existential threat and arguing that all the other issues discussed this election season were trivial in comparison.
On Wednesday, Netanyahu said he had sent a directive to Israel's security forces to topple Iran's clerical state.
A day earlier, he posted a video of himself in front of a fighter jet speaking to US President Donald Trump by phone saying they would "finish the job" together.--AFP

Title: Form Six allowance to be paid over 3 semesters

FORM Six students will receive a living allowance of RM2,500 starting next year, said Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek.
"The assistance, announced under the 2027 Budget, will be disbursed once registration for all Form Six students is completed."
Fadhlina said this after opening the "Jelajah Negaraku: Aku Kasih Malaysia" programme here yesterday.

Title: Trump: Audi to invest US$4.2b in first US plant
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump announced on Saturday that German automaker Audi planned to invest US$4.2 billion to build its first factory in the US that will produce 200,000 vehicles a year.
Audi said the plant would create about 4,500 jobs.
"I'm thrilled to announce a massive auto manufacturing investment in Georgia by a fantastic company," Trump said at a campaign rally.
The rally came 10 days before the Nov 3 midterm elections, which will determine control of the US Congress.
Audi, a subsidiary of Volkswagen, said construction was scheduled to begin next year and production in the early 2030s.
Audi said the investment would demonstrate its long-term commitment to the US and make North America a third major pillar of its global production network, alongside Europe and China.
Volkswagen has struggled with US tariffs, competition from Chinese manufacturers and uneven demand in Europe.
The Volkswagen Group has agreed to cut about 50,000 jobs, but the company has warned that a further 50,000 cuts could be needed worldwide to reduce costs.
